newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Acacia has record production in 2nd qtr.
newsitem.headline: Acacia has record production in 2nd qtr.

text.p: Gold miner Acacia Resources Ltd said on Thursday that its gold production in the second quarter was a record 117,673 ounces, a performance the company attributed to a strong debut from its Sunrise Dam mine.
Forecast gold production for the 1997 year had been increased to 400,000 ounces from 350,000 ounces previously.
Total costs for the quarter were A$366 per ounce, with a cash cost of A$287 per ounce. For the half year, total costs were A$398 per ounce, with cash costs of A$325.

Acacia said gold reserves at its wholly owned Union Reefs mine in the Northern Territory had been increased to 12 million tonnes at 1.97 gold grams per tonne (g/t). Its 40 percent owned Tanami Mine, also in the Northern Territory, increased resources by 13 percent to 920,000 ounces of which Acacia's share is 368,000 ounces.

During the quarter, Acacia said it had also divested its base metal interests. Principal among these was its interest in the Blendevale zinc-lead project in Western Australia which the company sold to Western Metals Ltd for a consideration of A$27 million and eight million Western Metals options exercisable at A$1.15 per share by the year 2002.

At Mt Fitch, the company said it had assigned its 51 interest in the copper, cobalt and nickel prospect to Compass Resources NL and the unlisted Guardian Resources NL. However, Acacia maintains a royalty interest in any production.
